issues.body:
The new 'CITE — Findings with rendered [source] citations (`--citations`, `sq-2489d.11`)' section instructs the reader to run `cargo run -p sparq-kb --features query --bin pkg-query -- --citations`. That flag is not implemented at the PR head.

Empirical verification (run at the PR head):
  $ cargo run -q -p sparq-kb --features query --bin pkg-query -- --citations
  pkg-query: unknown argument `--citations`
  <usage text>
  exit code 1

The crate compiles and the `pkg-query` bin resolves, so this is genuinely an unrecognised flag rather than a malformed invocation.

Source confirms it: the argument loop in crates/sparq-kb/src/bin/pkg_query.rs matches only `-h/--help`, `--list`, `--query`, `--sparql`, `--arg`, `--extra-graph`, `--close`, `--sparql-only`, `--json`, and ends with a catch-all `other => return Err(format!("unknown argument `{other}`"))`. Grepping `citations` in that file returns zero hits, and the `--help` usage block the PR does not update lists no such option.

Because SKILL.md is the agent-facing surface, this documentation will route agents to a command that always fails.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) include the implementation in this PR — add a `--citations` arm to the match in crates/sparq-kb/src/bin/pkg_query.rs that runs canned::FINDING_PROVENANCE.render(None), calls query::citations::render_citations, writes rendered citations to stdout and the metrics to stderr, and add the flag to the usage() text — or (b) drop this section until the implementing PR lands. Do not document a flag ahead of its implementation.
issues.title: Documents a `pkg-query --citations` CLI mode that does not exist; the documented command exits 1

issues.body:
The PR adds two references to `crates/sparq-kb/tests/pkg_query_cli.rs` — once as 'CLI gate:' at the end of the new CITE section, and once in the amended closing line ('Gates: crates/sparq-kb/tests/citations.rs and crates/sparq-kb/tests/pkg_query_cli.rs').

That file does not exist. `ls crates/sparq-kb/tests/pkg_query_cli.rs` returns 'No such file or directory', and a repo-wide `find . -name pkg_query_cli.rs -not -path ./target/*` returns nothing. The tests directory contains bd_bridge_eval.rs, citations.rs, core_connector.rs, dogfood_shacl.rs, extra_graph.rs, ingest_query.rs, ingest_shacl.rs, literature_pipeline.rs, nl_tool.rs, query_canned.rs, trust_graph_pkg.rs, yamlld_write_path.rs, and the fixtures/golden dirs — no pkg_query_cli.rs.

The 'Gate:' convention in this document exists so a reader can find the test that pins the documented behaviour. Pointing it at a non-existent file asserts verification coverage that was never written, which is materially worse than omitting the line: it makes an unimplemented, untested feature read as gated.
issues.fix_hint: Remove both references, or land the actual test file. If implementing, crates/sparq-kb/tests/pkg_query_cli.rs should assert non-vacuously: that `--citations` exits 0, that rendered `[source: label]` citations appear on stdout, that the metrics appear on stderr, and that each documented incompatible-flag combination exits non-zero. Assert on real process output, not a mocked helper that bypasses the CLI arg parsing.
issues.title: Cites a gate test file `crates/sparq-kb/tests/pkg_query_cli.rs` that does not exist in the repo

issues.body:
The final hunk rewrites an existing, correct line:

  -  Gate: `crates/sparq-kb/tests/citations.rs`.
  +  CLI mode: `pkg-query --citations`. Gates: `crates/sparq-kb/tests/citations.rs` and
  +  `crates/sparq-kb/tests/pkg_query_cli.rs`.

The original was true — crates/sparq-kb/tests/citations.rs exists and gates the library-level render_citations. The replacement pairs that true reference with a non-existent file and adds a 'CLI mode' claim that is false, so a correct doc line is degraded into a partly-false one. A reader who spot-checks the first path will find it valid and reasonably assume the second is too.

Worth stating clearly: the library layer this line originally described is genuinely present and appears sound — crates/sparq-kb/src/query/citations.rs defines render_citations, CitationReport and CitationMetrics; crates/sparq-kb/tests/citations.rs exists; and the `finding-provenance` canned query is defined at crates/sparq-kb/src/query/canned.rs:105. The defect is strictly the newly claimed CLI surface, not the underlying feature.
issues.fix_hint: Restore the line to `Gate: crates/sparq-kb/tests/citations.rs.` until the CLI mode and its test actually exist, then extend it in the PR that lands them.
issues.title: Amended closing line regresses a previously accurate 'Gate:' reference

issues.body:
Beyond the flag itself, the new section specifies a precise contract that no code implements:

1. 'always runs the unparameterised finding-provenance canned query and renders each Finding's prov:wasDerivedFrom source as a [source: label] citation'
2. 'Rendered citation text is written to stdout'
3. 'The executed-SPARQL banner and the MEASURED metrics — total citations, fabricated count, and citation-resolution rate — are written to stderr, mirroring the existing N row(s). convention'
4. 'Use --sparql-only to print the SPARQL without running it. --extra-graph and --close compose with citation mode as usual.'
5. 'The mode takes no argument: --query, --sparql, --arg, and --json are each incompatible and rejected with a non-zero exit.'
6. 'The NL-tool --json envelope carries no citation fields.'

None of these can hold, because parsing rejects `--citations` before any of this logic would run. Claim 5 in particular describes validation code that does not exist — pkg_query.rs contains only the `--query`/`--sparql` mutual-exclusion check, with no citation-mode conflict handling. Claim 3's metrics wording implies MEASURED output the CLI never produces.

This matters for the implementing PR too: a spec written before the code, with no test pinning it, is likely to drift from whatever is eventually built.
issues.fix_hint: When implementing, treat these six claims as the acceptance criteria and pin each with an assertion in the CLI test, especially the stdout/stderr split (claims 2-3) and every incompatible-flag rejection in claim 5. Verify the stderr metrics are computed from CitationMetrics rather than recomputed or hard-coded in the bin.
issues.title: Detailed behavioural contract for the CITE mode is entirely unbacked by code

verdict.summary: Doc-only PR to .claude/skills/query-pkg/SKILL.md that documents a `pkg-query --citations` CLI mode which DOES NOT EXIST at the PR head, and cites a gate test file that does not exist anywhere in the repo. Verified empirically, not by inspection alone: `cargo run -q -p sparq-kb --features query --bin pkg-query -- --citations` prints `pkg-query: unknown argument `--citations`` and exits 1. The binary builds and the bin name resolves, so the failure is genuinely the unrecognised flag, not a bad invocation. Source confirms it: the arg loop in crates/sparq-kb/src/bin/pkg_query.rs matches only --list/--query/--sparql/--arg/--extra-graph/--close/--sparql-only/--json with a catch-all `other => return Err(unknown argument)`; grep for `citations` in that file yields zero hits. The claimed gate `crates/sparq-kb/tests/pkg_query_cli.rs` is absent from crates/sparq-kb/tests/ and from a repo-wide find. Note the underlying LIBRARY is real and pre-existing: crates/sparq-kb/src/query/citations.rs (render_citations, CitationReport, CitationMetrics), its gate crates/sparq-kb/tests/citations.rs, and the canned query named `finding-provenance` (canned.rs:105) all exist. The defect is confined to the newly documented CLI surface. Consequently every behavioural claim in the new CITE section is unbacked: the stdout citation rendering, the stderr metrics banner (total citations / fabricated count / resolution rate), composition with --extra-graph/--close/--sparql-only, and the claimed rejection of --query/--sparql/--arg/--json as incompatible. There is no code implementing any of it. The amended closing line also regresses a previously accurate reference by appending the non-existent test to a correct one. SKILL.md is the agent-facing surface, so this actively routes agents to a command that exits 1. This fails the honesty rule that every documented claim trace to what the code actually does. Either land the implementation plus the gate test here, or drop the docs.
